title: Automate Posts to Instagram: How to Do It (2026 Guide)
summary: Automate posts to Instagram by starting with Meta's native scheduler. Know when to switch to third-party tools based on your specific business needs.
body_markdown:
## Stage 3: Automate publishing from a spreadsheet with Activepieces


If your team already keeps a content sheet, Activepieces can turn each new row into a published Instagram post through the official Instagram Business integration. Without a sheet, Stage 2 is enough.


You don't hire for this, you describe it: tell Activepieces' built-in chat that each new row in the sheet should become an Instagram post, and it builds and publishes the flow in your account.


What you get is an ordinary flow, no different from one built by hand, and it sits under the same access roles and audit logs as every other flow there. **Every run leaves a trace anyone can read** , showing which row became which post.


Meta's publishing rules still apply to it unchanged.


Because the action publishes through that connection, the Business or Creator account from the earlier stages is still required.


Five steps make up the build, and the order is fixed, meaning each run follows the identical path. The sheet comes first, since every later step reads from its columns.


1. Create the Sheet with image URL, caption and publish date columns.
2. Add the New Row trigger.
3. Add the Instagram Business publish action.
4. Map the three fields.
5. Test with one row.


Run them in that order, because each one depends on the step before it. The sections below take the connection, the mapping and the test in turn.


### Connect the sheet and Instagram


Start with the sheet, because the trigger reads its header row when you select it. Name the three columns plainly: image URL, caption and publish date. Then add the New Row trigger in Activepieces and authorise your Google account.


Add the Instagram Business publish action and sign in with the Facebook login linked to your Instagram account. If that login isn't tied to a Business or Creator account, the connection will fail here, so settle account type before you spend time on the workflow.


### Map spreadsheet columns to image URL and caption


Point each field the action asks for at a column the trigger supplies; that is mapping. The image URL column feeds the media field, and the caption column feeds the caption field.


Since Meta fetches the image from that address, the link must be publicly reachable and must lead to a file in a supported format. A link to a shared-drive preview page will fail.


Treat the publish date column, the third field, as your own control: the New Row trigger fires when you add a row, not when a date arrives.


**A future date in that column doesn't schedule anything by itself.** Add rows meant for later only when their date comes.


### Test the Instagram automation with one row


Add a single row with a real image link and a short caption, then run the test from the trigger step.


Check the post on the account itself, not only the green status in Activepieces, because a run can report success while a caption is truncated or an image is cropped.


If the post appears as intended, publish the flow. If it fails, the error names the step, which usually points to the image link or the account connection.


Once one row has gone through cleanly, the sheet can feed the account without further handling.
